newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers steady in quiet Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers steady in quiet Monday trade.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly little changed in typical Monday trade, brokers said.
They reported reasonable activity in the key Middle East sector, with the 255,000 tonne Torino fixed Kharg Island/Red Sea at W57.5 for BP.
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan were flat at about W60 and to the west at W55.
"I expect this week to be quite active, but not as active as last when people were returning to the market after IP Week," one broker said.

In the transatlantic sector the 380,000 tonne ultra-large crude carrier (ULCC) Marine Atlantic was fixed from Sullom Voe to the U.S. Gulf on March 10 for Glencore, which dominated buying in the wet Brent market last week.
Glencore was also said to have fixed on subjects the 330,000 tonne Arcadia from Sullom Voe to South Africa.

West Africa 130,000 tonners were fixed at a steady W100/105 to the U.S. Atlantic coast, with cross-Med rates about comparable. Cross-Med 80,000 tonnes edged down to W115 from about W120, brokers said.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonners were flat at W115/117.5 while fuel oil was also little changed at W205 for 20,000 tonnes and W200/205 cross-Med.
In the U.S. 70,000 tonnes upcoast was steady at W150, while 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil remained at W190 -- close to the average for the last week, one broker said.
